coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Potrero Power Station Block 1
record.summary: Planned mixed-use block on the Potrero Power Station masterplan with a stepped height envelope up to 180 ft, one of three blocks (with 5 and 13) eligible to host the project's single permitted district parking garage; no design review approval or construction start found.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land within the former power station site (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram by fitting it to multiple real street points, but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade, and treat the block's applicability itself as somewhat more provisional than Mission Rock's or Pier 70's equivalent entries. Rebuilt 2026-09-16 with control-point georeferencing. Re-measured 2026-09-16 (third revision) in a single consistent measurement across the whole block layout. Re-corrected 2026-09-16 (fourth revision) after a mis-measured control point was fixed. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record). The statement that the block is unbuilt, on vacant/graded land and unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll is our own observation (satellite imagery and the Assessor roll), not something the cited 2020 D4D can show; the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025) does not list a Block 1 application. The statement that the diagram is dated 2020 is confirmed by the final D4D's footer (February 26, 2020).
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of the site's larger, largely unaddressed footprint), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named blocks -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead. (This is our own reading of the parcel data, not something the cited Design for Development can establish; the D4D does not address Assessor parcels.) The 2018 draft EIR (Vol. 1, PDF p.107) says a portion of Block 1 lies within the PG&E sub-area, which is part of Assessor's Block 4175/Lot 018, so an unsubdivided Assessor lot does underlie part of this block.
notes.regulatory_context: Figure 6.2.3 of the final D4D (printed p.245) shows Block 1, marked '1*' (a potential district parking garage location up to 90 ft in height and potential grocery store location), in two height zones read from the figure's colour-coded labels: '180'/85'' on its west part (maximum height 180 ft, maximum base height 85 ft) and '85'' on its east part. The '115'MAX' marking on the figure is a plan-dimension line for the tower zone, not a height. The October 7, 2020 Phase 1 and Phasing Plan Amendment approval places Block 1 in Phase 2 and moves the option for space for a Public Library to Block 1 in Phase 2 (an option, not a committed branch). No construction-start source found.

changes.text: Block 1's heights now follow the colour-coded labels on the Design for Development's Figure 6.2.3 (180 ft maximum with an 85 ft base on the west part, 85 ft on the east part); the earlier '115 ft' was a plan-dimension line, not a height. The expected completion changed from the 2035 whole-project date to 2031: the October 2020 Phase 1 approval places Block 1 in Phase 2 and SocketSite's schedule table shows vertical development 2029-2031 (a 2020 forecast). The earlier statement that no source supports a Public Library option here was removed: the Phase 1 approval moves that option to Block 1. The dead August 2019 draft Design for Development link was replaced with the final February 2020 document, the land-use figure is now tagged as a document rather than a rendering, and publisher names on source entries were corrected.

open_questions: No design review approval or construction-start date found for Block 1; it is not one of the six buildings named in the 2024 annual compliance report's Phase 1 list (Blocks 2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15), and no later-phase design review approval was found either.

No source found claiming a specific planned use (e.g., grocery store) beyond the D4D's own generic 'Potential District Parking Garage Location, Potential Grocery Store Location' asterisk notation, which applies to Blocks 1, 5 and 13 collectively, not to Block 1 alone.

Block-specific schedule: the only one found is the 2020 forecast in SocketSite's table (Block 1 vertical development 2029-2031, Phase 2); no later schedule or design review approval for Block 1 was found, so the expected 2031 completion is a 2020 phase forecast only.
